statement.excerpt: I, personally, believe his estimate is too conservative — because it doesn’t factor in the capital expenditures from Oracle, which (along with Crusoe) is building the vast Abilene Texas data center for OpenAI, or any private data center developers sinking cash into AI capex.

from_speaker: doesn’t factor in the capital expenditures from Oracle
or any private data center developers
Context identifies approximately $520 billion for 2025, but also discusses $312 billion.
our_interpretation: Treat the assertion that the full-year estimate is too low as a forecast about calendar 2025, despite its observation label.
Use $520 billion as the proposed benchmark, while preserving the conflicting $312 billion reference as an unresolved ambiguity.
The surrounding discussion suggests US AI investment. Spending outside the United States cannot establish that total.
Support requires both an underestimate and the alleged omission. Developer spending must be counted without duplicating expenditure already captured through customers, equipment suppliers or leases.
‘I personally believe’ expresses confidence rather than an external condition.
criteria.support_condition: A consistent accounting shows that US AI capital expenditure in calendar 2025 exceeded $520 billion and that Oracle and private-developer investment omitted from Kedrosky’s calculation materially explains the underestimate.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable full-year spending was no greater than the benchmark, or the identified calculation demonstrably already incorporated the supposedly omitted investment.
